reasoning_content:
The circle has center O and diameter AB. The angles shown: 40° from OA (left side) to one radius, then the shaded sector between that radius and another radius, then 45° between that radius and another radius, and then 25° from that radius to OB.

Wait, let me look at the figure. The diameter AB is horizontal. From O, there are radii going into the upper half. Angles: 40° is between OA and the left green radius (the left boundary of the shaded sector). 25° is between OB and the right green radius. 45° is between the right green radius and the black radius (the right boundary of the shaded sector)? Wait, let me look again.

Figure: the shaded sector is between the left green radius (about 140° from positive x-axis) and the black radius (about 70°). The 45° label is between the black radius and the right green radius (about 25°). The 25° label is between the right green radius and OB (positive x-axis).

Angles on the upper side of the diameter: from OA (180°) to the left green radius: 40°. So the left green radius is at 180° - 40° = 140°. From OB (0°) to the right green radius: 25°, so the right green radius is at 25°. Between the right green radius and the black radius: 45°, so the black radius is at 25° + 45° = 70°.

Shaded sector: between the left green radius (140°) and the black radius (70°): angle = 140° - 70° = 70°.

Check: total of upper half: 40° + shaded + 45° + 25° = 180°, so shaded = 180 - 110 = 70°.

Probability = 70/360 = 7/36.

Therefore the answer: \boxed{7/36}.
content:
Looking at the upper half of the disk (the half above diameter AB), the angles along the straight line AB must sum to 180°.

The angles from A to B along the top are: 40° (from OA to the left edge of the shaded sector), the shaded sector's angle, 45°, and 25°.

So the shaded sector's central angle is:
180° − 40° − 45° − 25° = 70°

The probability that a uniformly chosen point lies in the shaded sector equals the ratio of the sector's angle to the full circle:
70° / 360° = 7/36

\boxed{7/36}
